captions.detailed: This 3D model is a tall, tapered handle with a circular cross-section, narrowing from a wider, rounded top to a smaller, rounded bottom. It features a central vertical hole running through its entire height, designed to accommodate a mounting screw. The top and bottom ends are smoothly filleted, giving the overall shape a sleek, ergonomic, and capsule-like appearance.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric tapered handle in OpenSCAD with rounded top and bottom ends. The user should be able to adjust the height, bottom width, top width, and the fillet radii for both ends, as well as customize the central screw hole dimensions for a secure bottom-up attachment.
captions.factory: The model is constructed using a difference() operation. The main body is created by applying hull() to two distinct tori: one at the bottom and one translated to the top, each generated using rotate_extrude() on a translated circle() to define the rounded caps. Two concentric cylinder() primitives are then subtracted from this main body along the Z-axis to form the countersunk screw shaft and head clearance holes.
